/// The quote the file `home` names holds at the offset `at` of its text, as the written item holding
/// it reads back: the store holding it and the quote; absent where none does.
fn written_quote(engine: QueryEngine, home: string, at: int) -> Scratch? {
    let file? = template_file(home) else { return null }
    let i? = quote_item(engine, file, at).first() else { return null }
    let store = read_item(engine, file, i).store
    let q? = store.quote_at(at - item_start(engine, file, i)) else { return null }
    Scratch { store: store, body: q }
}

/// The written item of `file` holding the quote at the offset `at` of its text, none where none
/// does: the item whose text holds the offset, where a quote stands there in it.
@query
fn quote_item(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> List<int> {
    [i for i in 0..item_count(engine, file) for start in [item_start(engine, file, i)] if start <= at &&
        at < start + item_under(engine, file, i).text.length &&
        read_item(engine, file, i).store.quote_at(at - start) != null]
        .take(1)
}

# Cloud lanes — how we use Claude Code web sandboxes

One lane = one cloud session = one sandbox = one branch. The lead (local Mac session) coordinates through the
`claude-web` bridge (`../claude_web_mcp`, README there is the tool reference).

## Names — one id everywhere

The bridge makes the name: `create_session {project: "avra", kind: "lane"|"ops", topic}` -> `avra-lane-<topic>`
(a taken name gets `-2`, `-3`). It sets the title and tells the agent its branch and file stem; nobody types a name.

| Where | Spelling |
|---|---|
| Cloud session title | `avra-lane-<topic>` |
| Git branch | `avra-lane-<topic>` |
| Bundle a lane hands back | `avra-lane-<topic>.bundle` |
| Lane note | `.lead/handoff/avra-lane-<topic>.md` |
| Non-lane sessions (builds, probes) | `avra-ops-<what>` |

## What a sandbox is

- Environment **Avra 2**: Ubuntu 24.04, 4 cores, 15 GB, no swap, 30 GB disk, ~2 min to start.
- Setup script leaves: LLVM 22, a built Linux compiler in `/opt/avra-tc`, the source at `/work/avra`
  (artifact `avra-work.tar.gz`: a shallow clone of `program` and open lane branches, ~150 MB — ke
…[1619 chars cut]…
 through the bridge.
- A lane touches only its own branch. Two lanes never own one file set — the brief names the files.
- Speed claims: exact counts plus `cmp` of products on one fixed source.
- Credentials in a sandbox's environment are never printed, posted or forwarded.
- The Mac gate is the bar for moving `program`; a cloud gate is the lane's own proof.

## Capacity

Each sandbox is its own machine, so lanes no longer compete for the Mac's memory or disk. The limit is the
lead's landing rate (one Mac gate per batch, merges serial), so lanes are cut by file ownership and landed in
batches.

/// In-process rolling hash; both operands normalized under a prime so
/// mixing never overflows, negative payloads included. The crypto
/// tier arrives with the on-disk cache.
fn fp_mix(h: int, v: int) -> int {
    mut nv = v % 1000000007
    if nv < 0 { nv = nv + 1000000007 }
    (h * 131 + nv + 7) % 1000000007
}

/// A text's fold: its bytes eight to a word, the tail byte by byte, then its length.
export fn fp_str(s: string) -> int {
    mut h = 0
    mut i = 0
    // A string's `.length` is a header load: asked once, not per word.
    let n = s.length
    while i + 8 <= n {
        h = fp_mix(h, avra_str_word_at(s, i))
        i = i + 8
    }
    while i < n {
        h = fp_mix(h, s.char_code(i))
        i = i + 1
    }
    fp_mix(h, n)
}

export fn item_key(text: string) -> string {
    let line? = text.split("\\n").find(names_item) else { return "" }
    let cut = [line.index_of(c) ?? line.length for c in ["(", "{", "=", "<", ":"]].fold(line.length, min_int)

    let code = line.trim()
    !code.is_empty() && !code.starts_with("//") && !code.starts_with("@")

fn impls_filed_in(engine: QueryEngine, package: string) -> bool {

/// `files`, the longest first, so processes taking turns share the work about evenly: a file's
/// length is read off its text, which costs nothing a build has not already read.
fn widest_first(engine: QueryEngine, files: List<SourceFileAddress>) -> List<SourceFileAddress> {
    let widths = [source_text(engine, f)?.length ?? 0 for f in files]
    [files[at] for at in sorted_by([at for at in 0..files.length], (a, b) -> widths[a] > widths[b])]
}

/// Where a union member is declared: its file, spelled after whether its package is the reader's,
/// and its place among the file's declarations; a type the language owns before every file.
type MemberPlace = { file: string, at: int }

fn member_place(engine: QueryEngine, t: SignedType, reader: string) -> MemberPlace {
    match t.head {
        .Declared(file, name) -> MemberPlace {
            file: "${if file.package_name == reader { 0 } else { 1 }}${file.package_name}:${file.path_in_package}",
            at: file_declares(engine, file).names.find_index(it.name == name) ?? -1,
        },
        rest -> MemberPlace { file: "", at: -1 },
    }
}

/// `fronts`, one after another.

/// What an item's statements say of one name they declare or bind, each by the first statement of
/// that name: whether one declares it; whether the first that declares it wears an annotation, and
/// is a component with a body; and whether the first that declares or binds it wears one.
@derive(Saved)
type NameWorn = { name: string, declared: bool, marked_declared: bool, marked: bool, bodied_component: bool }

/// What each name the statements `all` of `store` declare or bind wears, each name once, in the order
/// they're met.
fn names_worn(store: SyntaxArena, all: List<StmtId>) -> List<NameWorn> {
    let named = [n! for s in all for n in [store.declared_name(s) ?? store.let_name(s)] if n != null]
    [name_worn(store, all, n) for i, n in named if !named.take(i).contains(n)]
}

/// What `name` wears among the statements `all` of `store`.
fn name_worn(store: SyntaxArena, all: List<StmtId>, name: string) -> NameWorn {
    let declaring = all.find((s) -> store.declared_name(s) == name)
    let binding = all.find((s) -> store.declared_name(s) ?? store.let_name(s) == name)
    NameWorn {
        name: name,
        declared: declaring != null,
        marked_declared: declaring != null && !store.annotations_of(declaring!).is_empty(),
        marked: binding != null && !store.annotations_of(binding!).is_empty(),
        bodied_component: declaring != null && store.component_body(declaring!) != null,
    }
}

@cut_parted_query
fn item_summary(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> AnswerParts {

            NamedValue {
                name: SAID_PART,
                value: ItemSaid { runs: about.runs, worn: about.worn, declares: !declares.is_empty() }
                    .saved_bytes(),
            },
            NamedValue {
                name: DECLARES_PART,
                value: ItemDeclares { names: declares }.saved_bytes(),
            },
        ],
    )
}

}

}

## 3. Identity and keys (dense typed keys, #3)

- **Item id = (file id, declared signature key, occurrence)**, never position: a fn/type/const by its
  first declared name and kind; an impl by (target, trait); a run statement block by (kind, ordinal
  among unnamed items). Adding or removing an item renumbers nothing else.
- **A question is (phase, item id)**: two small ints. Answers live in per-phase column tables indexed by
  item id (answer hash, settled serial, value slot), so a reused ask is ONE array index plus a serial
  compare — this is engine steps 2/3/5: no argument folding, no hashed question lookup, no record box.
- Across processes the frontier keys questions by (phase, stable item key text) once per item, interned
  at load; in process everything is ints.

## 4. How reads are recorded

- Inside an item-phase: nothing is recorded; plain fns over the item's own syntax.
- At the boundary: an item-phase answer records the SUMMARY PARTS it read — (item id, name) → part
  hash — once per (reader, part), in the packed ReadTable (step 1, landed as 356be742). A read already
  recorded by this reader is skipped by a

export type HeldQuestion = { question: Question, settled_in: Cell<int>, answer: Cell<ContentHash>, parts: Cell<PartsFound?> }

/// The parts of one answer read so far, by the hash of each part's name: kept for the answer they
/// were found in alone, so an answer that moves finds every part afresh.
type PartsFound = { answer: ContentHash, by_name: HashKeyedTable<PartFound> }

/// A part found in an answer: what a read of it sees, and what it holds, absent for no such part.
type PartFound = { seen: PartSeen, value: Bytes? }

/// `question`, held, settled in no engine yet.
fn held_question(question: Question) -> HeldQuestion {
    HeldQuestion { question: question, settled_in: Cell.new(-1), answer: Cell.new(unanswered()), parts: Cell.new(null) }
}

impl HeldQuestion {
    /// The part named by the hash `name` found in `answer` before, absent when none was.
    fn part_found(answer: ContentHash, name: ContentHash) -> PartFound? {
        let found? = self.parts.get() else { return null }
        if !found.answer.same_as(answer) { return null }
        found.by_name.get(name)
    }

    /// `part`, found in `answer`, kept for the reads of it after; the parts found in an answer
    /// before it are let go.
    fn part_kept(answer: ContentHash, name: ContentHash, part: PartFound) -> PartFound {
        let was = self.parts.get()
        let found = if was != null && was!.answer.same_as(answer) { was! } else {
            let fresh = PartsFound { answer: answer, by_name: hash_keyed_table() }
            self.parts.set(fresh)
            fresh
        }
        found.by_name.put(name, part)
        part
    }
}

### 2026-11-19T21:56:52 AGENT
The part-read change is committed and building in the background (two passes, gen-2), over this design:
- **Held question:** a part door now asks the held question for its arguments, the same path the whole-answer wrapper already uses. It no longer saves and hashes its arguments on every read.
- **Cache key:** each held question keeps the parts it has found, keyed by the hash of the part's name and tagged with the hash of the answer they came from. If an edit moves that answer, the hash no longer matches and every part is looked up again, so a stale part can't be served.
- **Read records:** every read is still recorded exactly as before, cached or not, so read records don't change.

Once the build finishes I'll run a paired cold comparison against deff18ad, with findings diffed. Then I'll put the plain `item_held` change back on top of the cache and measure again, then do warm rows and the warm == cold witness on every edit section.

The `fn_signature` change is building gen-2, and the warm rows run straight after. Where the two targets stand:

- **Dense keys:** the deferral and the measurement are written into the design's keys section, at /work/handoff/meas/ITEM_PHASE_DESIGN.md.
- **`fn_signature`:** it now asks `faced_signature(file, at, name, face)`, using the face hash the declaration already carries. Reading the item back inside it isn't recorded as one of its reads, so only the reads its type resolution makes count. Queries computed during that read-back still record their own reads. A body edit leaves the face, and so the question and its reads, standing, so the literal and body rows should each drop by 1.
- **`file_instances`:** this one can't come off the floor. Instances need the item parsed with its context, and every per-item answer reads the meant tape, which itself reads `file_instances`. A per-item `item_instances` would only re-run in its place, so the count stays the same.

    }
    let _ = store.saved()
    Named { names: names, asked: engine.computed_queries() }
}

file_path: /work/wt-3/packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/tests/faced_signature_test.av
--- content ---
// A fn's signature asked of its declaration's face, attacked: each thing a signature reads from its
// own item edited with the body left alone moves the face, so the question, and the answer asked
// again where the old one was kept is the answer asked afresh. A body edited moves neither.
use compiler.{FnSignature, avra_fact_definitions, avra_source_world, file_declares, fn_signature}
use @std.program.answer_record.{ContentHash, content_hash}
use @std.program.disk_store.{disk_store_at}
use @std.program.query_engine.{query_engine}
use @std.program.source_facts.{use_source_world}
use compiler.tests.support.{file_at, files, list_held, read_held, store_dir}

const LIB: string = "export trait Shown {\n    fn shown() -> string\n}\n\nexport alias Num = int\n"

/// The file asked of, `f` declared in it as `head`, with a body no edit here touches.
fn main_with(head: string) -> string { "use lib.{Shown, Num}\n\nalias Here = int\n\n${head} { xs }\n\nfn g() -> int { 1 }\n" }

const PLAIN: string = "fn f<T>(xs: int, b: int) -> int"

/// One process asking `f`'s signature: its saved bytes' hash, `f`'s face, and the queries it ran.
type Asked = { signature: ContentHash, face: ContentHash?, ran: List<string> }

fn asked(dir: string) -> Asked {
    use_source_world(avra_source_world(read_held, list_held, "avra-test"))
    let store = disk_store_at(dir)
    let engine = query_engine(store, avra_fact_definitions())
    let file = file_at("src/main.av")
    let signature: FnSignature? = fn_signature(engine, file, "f")
    let face = file_declares(engine, file).names.find(it.name == "f")?.face
    let _ = store.saved()
    Asked {
        signature: content_hash(signature?.saved_bytes() ?? "absent".bytes()),
        face: face,
        ran: engine.computed_queries(),
    }
}

/// `f` written as `before` and asked, then written as `after` and asked again where the first
/// answers were kept (warm), and asked in a store that never saw `before` (cold).
type Attacked = { before: Asked, warm: Asked, cold: Asked }

fn attacked(name: string, before: string, after: string) -> Attacked {
    files().set({"src/lib/shapes.av": LIB, "src/main.av": main_with(before)})
    let dir = store_dir("${name}_warm")
    let first = asked(dir)
    files().put("src/main.av", main_with(after))
    let warm = asked(dir)
    let cold = asked(store_dir("${name}_cold"))
    Attacked { before: first, warm: warm, cold: cold }
}

impl Attacked {
    /// Whether the edit moved `f`'s face, and the answer asked warm is the answer asked cold.
    fn face_moved_and_agrees() -> bool {
        !same(self.before.face, self.warm.face) &&
            same(self.warm.face, self.cold.face) &&
            self.warm.signature.same_as(self.cold.signature)
    }

    /// As `face_moved_and_agrees`, and the answer moved too.
    fn answer_moved() -> bool { self.face_moved_and_agrees() && !self.before.signature.same_as(self.warm.signature) }
}

fn same(a: ContentHash?, b: ContentHash?) -> bool {
    let x? = a else { return b == null }
    let y? = b else { return false }
    x.same_as(y)
}

spec "a fn's signature, asked of its face" {
    given "a parameter's type edited" {
        then "the face, the question and the answer move, warm as cold" {
            attacked("param_type", PLAIN, "fn f<T>(xs: int, b: string) -> int").answer_moved()
        }
    }
    given "a default added to a parameter" {
        then "the face, the question and the answer move, warm as cold" {
            attacked("default_added", PLAIN, "fn f<T>(xs: int, b: int = 2) -> int").answer_moved()
        }
    }
    given "a parameter's default edited" {
        then "the face moves, and the answer asked warm is the one asked cold" {
            attacked("default_edited", "fn f<T>(xs: int, b: int = 2) -> int", "fn f<T>(xs: int, b: int = 3) -> int")
                .face_moved_and_agrees()
        }
    }
    given "a type parameter's bound added" {
        then "the face, the question and the answer move, warm as cold" {
            attacked("bound", PLAIN, "fn f<T: Shown>(xs: int, b: int) -> int").answer_moved()
        }
    }
    given "a seat marked `mut`" {
        then "the face, the question and the answer move, warm as cold" {
            attacked("seat_mut", PLAIN, "fn f<T>(xs: int, mut b: int) -> int").answer_moved()
        }
    }
    given "a seat marked `const`" {
        then "the face, the question and the answer move, warm as cold" {
            attacked("seat_const", PLAIN, "fn f<T>(xs: int, const b: int) -> int").answer_moved()
        }
    }
    given "the fn exported" {
        then "the face moves, and the answer asked warm is the one asked cold" {
            attacked("exported", PLAIN, "export ${PLAIN}").face_moved_and_agrees()
        }
    }
    given "the fn made `once`" {
        then "the face moves, and the answer asked warm is the one asked cold" {
            attacked("once", "fn f<T>() -> int", "once fn f<T>() -> int").face_moved_and_agrees()
        }
    }
    given "the answer spelled through the file's own alias" {
        then "the face, the question and the answer move, warm as cold" {
            attacked("local_alias", PLAIN, "fn f<T>(xs: int, b: int) -> Here").answer_moved()
        }
    }
    given "the answer's type edited" {
        then "the face, the question and the answer move, warm as cold" {
            attacked("answer", PLAIN, "fn f<T>(xs: int, b: int) -> string").answer_moved()
        }
    }
    given "the file's alias the answer is spelled through edited, the fn itself not" {
        then "the face stands, and the answer moves, warm as cold" {
            let edit = attacked(
                "alias_target",
                "fn f<T>(xs: int, b: int) -> Here",
                "fn f<T>(xs: int, b: int) -> Here",
            )
            files().put(
                "src/main.av",
                main_with("fn f<T>(xs: int, b: int) -> Here").replace("alias Here = int", "alias Here = string"),
            )
            let dir = store_dir("alias_target_warm")
            let warm = asked(dir)
            let cold = asked(store_dir("alias_target_cold2"))
            same(edit.warm.face, warm.face) &&
                warm.signature.same_as(cold.signature) &&
                !edit.warm.signature.same_as(warm.signature)
        }
    }
    given "a type parameter added" {
        then "the face, the question and the answer move, warm as cold" {
            attacked("tparam", PLAIN, "fn f<T, U>(xs: int, b: int) -> int").answer_moved()
        }
    }
    given "the body alone edited" {
        then "the face stands, and neither the signature nor its face's question is asked again" {
            files().set({"src/lib/shapes.av": LIB, "src/main.av": main_with(PLAIN)})
            let dir = store_dir("body")
            let before = asked(dir)
            files().put("src/main.av", main_with(PLAIN).replace("{ xs }", "{ xs + 1 }"))
            let after = asked(dir)
            same(before.face, after.face) &&
                before.signature.same_as(after.signature) &&
                !after.ran.contains("faced_signature") &&
                !after.ran.contains("fn_signature")
        }
    }
}

Once gen-2 is in, `build/avra test <file>` will run the spec alone. Meanwhile, here's the field-by-field diff of the face against `declared_signature`'s inputs:

| signature input (`WrittenFn` / `Signing`) | read from | in the face? |
|---|---|---|
| type params, bounds | `FnDecl.tparams` | written (not `@hollow`) |
| params: name, type, default, promises (`mut`/`const`), state, spread, marks | `FnDecl.params` (`Param` fields) | written; only `Param.id` is `@local` (carried, not a meaning) |
| answer type and its width | `FnDecl.ret` | written |
| extern params/ret | `ExternFn` fields | written |
| `writer` (a template's file) | `store.stmt_origins` | `@taped` stmt side table, written into the tape's own stream |
| `once`/`mutating`/`static`/`host` | facets | side-table facts, which the face hashes (signature doesn't read them) |
| what names resolve to | engine reads (`alias_target`, the module's names…) | not the item's: recorded as ever |
| body | `FnDecl.body` | `@hollow`, left out, and no signature reads it |

The attack spec checks each row in practice. I'll run it as soon as the build finishes.

### 2026-11-20T00:49:10 AGENT
The face-keyed signature passes your attack. Nothing has landed yet: the plain-`fn_signature` follow-up is building gen-2, and the full gate runs after.

**What was attacked.** I diffed the face against everything the signature reads from its own item, field by field. Only the fn body is left out of the face, and no signature input comes from the body. The new spec (`tests/faced_signature_test.av`, a5ff692b) edits one input at a time and leaves the body alone. For every edit, the face moves, and the answer asked in a store that saw the old version equals the answer asked in a fresh store:

| edit | does the answer move? |
|---|---|
| a parameter's type | yes |
| a default added | yes |
| a type parameter's bound | yes |
| a type parameter added | yes |
| a seat's `mut` | yes |
| a seat's `const` | yes |
| the answer's type | yes |
| the answer spelled through the file's own alias of a different type | yes |
| a default's value edited | no, the signature only says whether a default exists |
| `export` | no, the signature doesn't hold it |
| `once` | no, the signature doesn't hold it |
| the answer spelled through an alias of the same type | no, an alias resolves to what it names |

Two more cases check the boundary. Editing the alias itself leaves the face of `f` standing and still moves the answer, because the read of the alias stays a recorded read. A body-only edit leaves the face standing and doesn't re-ask `faced_signature`.

**Mutation check.** With the face held constant, 8 of the 14 cases fail: every case where the answer moves. So the spec catches a face that misses a signature input.

**Not attacked.** One input isn't covered by an edit test: a template's file of origin, for a fn that a template wrote. It's in the face by construction, because the origin is a side table written into the tape itself. But no test moves a template to another file.

**One fix along the way.** The first run failed one case: `-> int` changed to `-> Here`, where `Here` aliases `int`. The face moved but the answer stayed `int`, so the expectation was wrong, not the face. I split it into a same-type and a different-type alias case.

**Warm rows.** With the face-keyed signature, literal went 14 → 13 and body 15 → 14. But signature, added and renamed each rose by 1–2, because both `fn_signature` and `faced_signature` re-ran when the face moved. The follow-up makes `fn_signature` a plain fn, so only `faced_signature` re-runs. Both spec files pass, 21/21, from source.

**`file_instances` stays.** It needs each item parsed with its context, and every per-item answer is built on the meant tape, which reads `file_instances` itself. A per-item replacement would only re-run in its place, so the count wouldn't change.

When the build finishes I'll have the warm rows, a paired cold run with findings diffed, and then the full gate. After that comes the list of remaining asks, each marked irreducible or not.

/// A text's tokens, as Avra's grammar says they work.
export fn avra_columns(text: string) -> TokenColumns { token_columns(text, lex_source(text).tokens, avra().roles, avra_lexeme()) }

/// One item's tree on a tape, read from its text under its file's words: its statements, then
/// what its file keeps of it, its refusals among them.
export fn avra_item_tape(item_text: string, context: Bytes) -> SyntaxTape {
    let parsed = parse_program(avra(), new_source_file("<item>", item_text), context_words(context))
    tape_of_item(parsed.store, [s for s in parsed.stmts if !parsed.store.is_hoisted(s)])
}

/// An item's tape: its statements, what its file keeps of it, and every name it declares, what it
/// hoisted among them, each with its face.
export fn tape_of_item(store: SyntaxArena, stmts: List<StmtId>) -> SyntaxTape {
    mut tape = tape_writer()
    tape.count(stmts.length)
    for s in stmts { Stmt.taped_id(store, tape, s) }

    tape.said_about(item_about(store, stmts))
    tape.finished()
}

const APP: string = "[package]\nname = \"app\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n"

/// The package: `main` beside the library file, and a sibling in the library's module where given.
fn grain_package(main: string, lib: string, sibling: string?) -> Held {
    mut files = {"/w/avra.toml": APP, "/w/src/main.av": main, "/w/src/lib/a.av": lib}

/// What a second process works out judging `main` after the library goes from `before` to
/// `after`, over the store the first left.
fn reworked(main: string, before: string, after: string, sibling: string?, sibling_after: string?) -> List<
    string,
> {
    let store = empty_store()
    let _ = grain_package(main, before, sibling).worked_judging(grain_main(), store)
    grain_package(main, after, sibling_after).worked_judging(grain_main(), store)
}

//! `avra explain` — each form over a package of two files, as the command runs
//! where the package stands: every refusal whose words are about the argument,
//! a file's, a declaration's and one answer's page, the table, the calls of a
//! body, and the two properties an inspection owes — asked twice it prints the
//! same thing, and it leaves the store as it found it. `avra_ran`,
//! `avra_ran_in`, `scratch_dir` and `exit_is_zero` are the neighbouring tests'
//! own: this module shares one namespace.
use @std.io.{list_dir, make_dirs, write_text}
use @std.time.{stamp}
use @std.text.{parse_int}
/// A package of an entry and a module it imports, nothing built or checked yet.
fn probe(name: string) -> string {
    let root = "${scratch_dir()}/explain_${name}_${stamp()}"
    let _ = make_dirs("${root}/src/lib")
    let _ = write_text("${root}/avra.toml", "[package]\nname = \"probe\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n")
    let _ = write_text("${root}/src/lib/a.av", "export fn twice(n: int) -> int { n + n }\n")
    let _ = write_text(
        "${root}/src/main.av",
        "use lib.{twice}\n\nfn shown(n: int) -> string { \"\${twice(n)}\" }\n\nprintln(shown(4))\n",
    )
    root
}
/// The probe, checked: its store holds a check's answers.
fn checked(name: string) -> string {
    let root = probe(name)
    let _ = avra_ran(["check", root])
    root
}
/// What a form prints where it answers, absent where it refuses.

/// What a made item read back is held under: its file, its place, and its whole tape's print —
/// places included, so a template that moves makes another key.
export fn made_key(file: SourceFileAddress, at: int, tape: SyntaxTape) -> string {
    let print = content_hash(tape.saved_bytes())
    "${spelled_file(file)}#${at}#made#${print.high_word}:${print.low_word}"
}

/// The item `key` names, read back from the tape `placed` answers: the one held under the key, else
/// read and held. `key` names its content — a written item's text, a made one's whole tape — so two
/// items share an entry only where they read back alike.
fn held_read(key: string, placed: fn() -> PlacedTape, at: int?) -> ReadItem {
    if !items_held() { return item_whole(placed(), at) }
    let kept = held_items().get(key)
    if kept != null { return kept! }
    let before = avra_mem_live()
    let read = item_whole(placed(), at)
    held_items().put(key, read, avra_mem_live() - before)
    read
}

/// An item's tape read back into a store of its own: its statements, then each declaration it
/// hoists, which a read by name finds as it finds the written ones.
fn item_whole(placed: PlacedTape, at: int?) -> ReadItem {
    let store = new_node_store()
    let stmts = item_read_back(store, placed)
    ReadItem {
        store: store,
        stmts: stmts.concat(store.hoisted_decls()),
        written: store.expr_count(),
        at: at,
    }
}

The lead asked for the finding as soon as I had it, so here it is. The proposed fix has one open question, which I'll test before building on it.

<to_controller>
warm: (b) done. 8266fe6c reverts the summary merge and keeps the split. Gen-2, warm rows and the full gate are running detached; base58..HEAD goes out once base58 arrives.
Finding: it isn't a second engine. --findings makes one engine. The summary's 39.6k answers vs 22.9k written items are asks that never read back (the read is guarded to written ids).
Cause: read-back items sit in a 320 MB least-recently-used cache (held_items, HELD_BYTES). item_read_parts was asked during each item's laws, so laws hit the same read-back.
The merged summary is asked in the names phase over every item. It reads all 22.9k back early, the cache evicts them, and the laws read them back again.
Proof: with AVRA_HELD_BYTES=3e9, fix58 81.3/81.4 s vs merge 80.9/83.4 s, about +1% (noise). Default bound: +2-4%. Peak memory +270 MB.
The 320 MB bound also costs fix58 itself about 5 s (81 vs 85-87 s), a separate win if memory allows.
Proposed fix, both wins: build front, lets and seats where the tape is made (tape_of_item already has the parse store and stmts, as item_about does) and carry them on the tape's about. Then the summary reads them without any read-back.
Open question: "refused" is builder refusals on the read-back store. I'll check per item that the store the tape is made from carries the same set before relying on it.
If it does, the merge returns with literal 11 and cold level. If not, refused stays in item_read_parts and the merge saves nothing; I'll report either way.
</to_controller>

fn read_said(store: SyntaxArena, stmts: List<StmtId>) -> ItemReadSaid {

unsigned_at() {
    bin=$1; out=$2; shift 2
    if layered; then
        built="$(dirname "$(dirname "$bin")")/.avra-cache/tapes-build"
        for k in $(for f in "$built"/layers/*/keys.txt; do cat "$f"; echo; done | sort); do
            digest < "$built/obj/$k.o"
        done > "$out"
        for words in "$@"; do
            said=0
            "$bin" $words >> "$out" 2>&1 || said=$?
            echo "exit $said" >> "$out"
        done
    else
        cp "$bin" "$out"; codesign --remove-signature "$out" 2>/dev/null || :
    fi
}

# AN INSTANCE'S CHECK READS WHAT ITS RUN CALLS, AND NOTHING IT ONLY HOLDS: a component whose `check`

log=open(sys.argv[1]).read()

for m in re.finditer(r"argument (\d+) of `([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)` wants `int`, found `ItemId`", log):
    want[m.group(2)].add(int(m.group(1)))
files=[f for r in roots for f in glob.glob(r+'/**/*.av', recursive=True) if '/tests/' not in f]
done=0
for f in files:
    s=open(f).read(); orig=s
    for name,args in want.items():
        for m in list(re.finditer(r'\bfn '+re.escape(name)+r'(<[^>]*>)?\(', s)):
            i=m.end(); depth=1; j=i
            while depth and j<len(s):
                if s[j] in '([{<': depth+=1
                elif s[j] in ')]}>': depth-=1
                j+=1
            params=s[i:j-1]
            parts=[]; d=0; cur=''
            for ch in params:
                if ch in '([{<': d+=1
                if ch in ')]}>': d-=1
                if ch==',' and d==0: parts.append(cur); cur=''
                else: cur+=ch
            if cur.strip(): parts.append(cur)
            # argument numbering counts the receiver-less params; engine is argument 1
            changed=False
            for a in args:
                k=a-1
                if k < len(parts) and re.search(r':\s*int\s*$', parts[k]):
                    parts[k]=re.sub(r':\s*int\s*$', ': ItemId', parts[k]); changed=True
            if changed:
                s=s[:i]+','.join(parts)+s[j-1:]; done+=1
    if s!=orig: open(f,'w').write(s)
print('retyped', done, 'of', len(want))
EOF

/// A BODY'S FRAMES PLACED IN THEIR FILES: a frame laid out by its item counts its site from the
/// item's start, and here, once, from its file's (`file_placed`). A chunk's module reads a frame
/// another module defines, so no chunk holds a place in its file.
fn placed_frames(engine: QueryEngine, b: LoweredFn) -> LoweredFn { b with { statics: [placed_frame(engine, s) for s in b.statics] } }

fn placed_frame(engine: QueryEngine, s: Static) -> Static {
    let at? = s.at_item else { return s }
    let file? = home_file(engine, s.home) else { return s }
    let site? = s.boxes.first() else { return s }
    let cells? = slots_of(site) else { return s }
    if cells.length != 3 { return s }
    let lo? = slot_int(cells[1]) else { return s }
    let hi? = slot_int(cells[2]) else { return s }
    let placed = file_placed(engine, file, at, FindingAt { lo: lo, hi: hi })
    s with { boxes: [StaticBox.Slots([cells[0], Slot.Int(placed.lo), Slot.Int(placed.hi)])].concat(s.boxes.drop(1)), at_item: null }
}

fn slots_of(b: StaticBox) -> List<Slot>? { match b { .Slots(cells) -> cells, rest -> null } }

/// Whether `d`, a declaration of `kind`, is declared after the written item `at` of `file`: in a
/// file whose path comes later, or later in the same file.
fn declared_after(
    engine: QueryEngine,
    d: DeclaredAt,
    kind: ItemKind,
    file: SourceFileAddress,
    at: ItemId,
) -> bool {
    if !same_file(d.file, file) { return text_before(file.path_in_package, d.file.path_in_package) }
    let item = file_declares_named(engine, d.file, d.name)
        .names

/// Whether the union member `a` stands before `b`, as the package `reader` reads them.
fn member_before(engine: QueryEngine, a: SignedType, b: SignedType, reader: string) -> bool {
    let pa = member_place(engine, a, reader)
    let pb = member_place(engine, b, reader)
    if pa.file != pb.file { return text_before(pa.file, pb.file) }
    if pa.at != pb.at { return pa.at < pb.at }
    text_before(a.spelled(), b.spelled())
}

/// Where a union member is declared: its file, spelled after whether its package is the reader's,
/// and its place among the file's declarations; a type the language owns before every file.
type MemberPlace = { file: string, at: int }

fn member_place(engine: QueryEngine, t: SignedType, reader: string) -> MemberPlace {
    match t.head {
        .Declared(file, name) -> MemberPlace {
            file: "${if file.package_name == reader { 0 } else { 1 }}${file.package_name}:${file.path_in_package}",
            at: file_declares(engine, file).names.find_index(it.name == name) ?? -1,

/// What an item says that its reading back says too (`read_said`).
@derive(Saved)
type ItemReadSaid = { front: ItemFront, refused: bool, lets: List<string>, seats: List<SeatsNamed> }

/// Which seats of the fn `name` are `mut`, in order.
@derive(Saved)
type SeatsNamed = { name: string, mutable: List<bool> }

/// What a tape made before an item said what its reading back says, says: nothing.
fn no_read_said() -> ItemReadSaid { ItemReadSaid { front: no_front(), refused: false, lets: [], seats: [] } }

/// What an item writes that the items after it read, where it writes nothing.
fn no_front() -> ItemFront { ItemFront { binds: [], uses: [] } }

/// `said` as parts: `front`, `refused`, `lets`, and `w<name>` for each fn's seats.
fn read_parts(said: ItemReadSaid) -> List<NamedValue> {

        .concat([NamedValue { name: seats_part(x.name), value: SeatsMarked { mutable: x.mutable }.saved_bytes() } for x in said.seats])
}

    item_read_parts_part(engine, file, at, name)

### 2026-11-20T22:06:10 AGENT
On a cache hit a plain part read still pays per ask:
- the caller's name string;
- `part_name.bytes()`, an allocation;
- a blake3 hash of the name;
- the part cache probe;
- a `RecordedRead` record.

Removing the string and the hash would mean naming parts by a fold of ints instead of a hashed string. That changes how every parted answer names its parts, an engine-wide change with store compatibility to manage. And the per-ask read record stays either way, because it's how the dependency gets recorded. So the cut query is the realistic fix for 58, and the numbers for its price are above. I'll wait for 57's measurement to attribute the rest.

### 2026-11-20T22:24:05 AGENT
On the cost P0, the sites the lead listed are mine, and two fixes are now committed on the 58 head (290e28de). Neither can be sent yet under the new cost rule.

**What each site does per call**
- `held_part` is the cost of `item_held` being a plain part read: every ask spells the part name `"h${at}"`, and it's asked from about 124 places.
- `part_of_answer_held`, `hash.held` and `octets_at` come from my engine path: every part read turns the name into bytes, hashes it, and builds a new read record.
- `declaration_of` is the signature lookup, which builds a declaration record and filters the file's declarations by name.

My earlier timing check said plain `item_held` was free, but this slice counts allocations, and these sites are where they churn.

**Fix 1 (b28eb1ec): `item_held` is a cut query again.** Its part is read once per item, and later asks are a cheap probe. Against base 451aaeb2 on this machine:
- boxes fell 1.8–2.8% and retains 1.3–1.9% on every workload;
- 21 rows are still over the 0.05% tolerance (26 lowered): `queries_computed` +5.8% on check-cli and +1.9% on check-program (`item_held`'s answers counted again, as in 57), `empty_opens` about +0.9%, and copies and string compares +0.1–0.2%.

**Fix 2 (bb8a9368): a part read already found allocates nothing.** The cache is probed by an allocation-free fold of the part name, with the stored name compared so a collision can't serve the wrong part. Each cached part also keeps its read record, so a repeat read reuses it. This targets the remaining 4.2M part reads on build-cli, at three allocations each.

**Measurement note.** 57 measured here matches the committed baseline almost exactly, so the counts aren't machine-dependent. Base 451aaeb2 is +28% boxes over 57 on build-cli here. That presumably includes the regression ui-language's fix removed on the lead's head, which is why the lead sees +4.1%.

Running now, detached and alone: bb8a9368 built gen-1 by the batch-57 compiler, then gen-2, the cost slice and the judge against 451aaeb2, then edit-c and avrac-a. If rows are still over tolerance afterwards, I'll name the remaining cost for the lead to take to the owner.

The cold-build P0 fix is committed as 798eaa93, on 7670816d for now: 0f278326 isn't here yet. I've asked the lead for it.

The fix: when this process has just computed a parted answer, or has its value held in memory, a part read now takes the part straight from that in-memory value. It no longer decodes the parts table from the answer's saved bytes. Answers that came from the store, from another process or a warm run, are still read from their bytes as before, and every part read is recorded the same way, so warm reuse doesn't change. `check` is clean for std-program and cli.
